scenes.text: How ChatGPT knows today's news. Ask ChatGPT about something that happened this morning, and it still answers, with links. [1] But wait, wasn't it trained months ago? [2] Let's break down how AI searches the web for you.

title: AI Web
Search
data.subtitle: How ChatGPT answers with fresh info

scenes.text: Here's the problem. [1] An LLM only knows what was in its training data, and that stops at a certain date, called the knowledge cutoff. [2] With web search, it can look things up live, so it knows what happened today.

left.title: Without search
left.label: knows only up to its cutoff

scenes.text: Here's what happens, in seconds. [1] You ask, who won yesterday's cricket match? [2] The model sees it needs fresh information, so it calls a search tool. [3] The search returns the top results, [4] the system reads the best pages, and pulls out the key parts, [5] and the model writes the answer, with links to its sources.

Notice something? This combines two ideas you already know. [1] Tool use, from episode nine, because searching is a tool the model calls. [2] And RAG, from episode seven, because it retrieves information, and adds it to the prompt. [3] Put them together, and you get an AI that's up to date.

data.heading: Two ideas, combined
steps: The model calls a search tool (EP 09)
Found pages go into the prompt (EP 07)

scenes.text: Let's watch it happen. [1] You ask, what's the gold price in India today? [2] The model writes a search, gold price India today. [3] It gets back three fresh sources, updated this morning. [4] And it answers with today's rate, and shows you the links, so you can check them.

data.heading: Web search, live
data.question: What's the gold price in India today?
data.answer: Here's today's rate, based on these 3 sources. Tap a link to see the details.

scenes.text: A few smart habits. [1] Check the sources, open at least one link. [2] Look at the dates, old pages give old answers. [3] For anything important, ask for more than one source. [4] And remember, if the pages are wrong, the answer can be wrong too.

Where will you see this? [1] ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity can all search the web. [2] Google shows AI overviews at the top of search results. [3] And shopping assistants compare prices across stores.

data.heading: Where you'll see it
items: AI overviews on top of results

scenes.text: Here's a common myth. [1] People think the AI already knows everything on the internet. [2] It doesn't. Without search, it only knows its training data, and with search, it reads just a handful of pages each time.

data.myth: The AI already knows everything on the internet.
data.fact: Without search it only knows its training data. With search, it reads a handful of pages each time.

Let's recap. [1] LLMs are frozen at their knowledge cutoff. [2] Web search is a tool the model calls. [3] The results go into the prompt, just like RAG. [4] And you should always check the sources. [5] Next, use case 3, how AI meeting notes work. Follow AI Maastaaru!
